newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania foreign investment decree clears parliament.
newsitem.headline: Romania foreign investment decree clears parliament.

text.p: A Romanian government decree on foreign investments has won parliamentary approval on Friday, clearing the way for fresh capital inflows.

The decree, endorsed by parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies after the Senate passed it last month, amends and completes a 1991 law on foreign inflows, granting incentives to direct and portfolio investors.
The new rules were published in the Official Gazette two weeks ago but needed parliament approval to become a law.
New incentives are granted for greenfield investments with a starting capital of at least $350,000, compared to a previous figure of $50 million.

They include exemptions from import duties for machinery, equipment and installations needed in investment projects and cuts in customs duties for imports of raw materials, machinery and spare parts in the first two years of activity.
Under the new rules, the profits tax paid by companies with a minimum 20 percent foreign participation would be 15 percent in the first two years of operation, compared with the current 38 percent.
A distinct chapter on portfolio investment sets a tax of up to 1.5 percent on each portfolio deal and guarantees repatriation of initial investments and capital gains.
Foreign investors and analysts have hailed the new rules, saying they were consolidating the investment framework, rolling out a red carpet for foreign investors.

Foreign investment has been thinner in Romania than elsewhere in Eastern Europe, with the country attracting a little over $2.3 billion in direct investment in seven years since the fall of communism.

Portfolio investors penetrated the Romanian capital market only this year after pledges by the new centrist government, which came into office in elections last November, of support to foreign investors and capital market growth.
A bill on local investment is expected to be discussed in parliament next week.
